title: Le Blanc: their modesty deserves praise; to define the manner of concurrence is rash
source_text: LV. Quantum ad me attinet, horumce Doctissimorum Virorum modestiam maxime laudandam censeo: & modum divini concursus, quo cum causis secundis prima cooperatur, pro certo definire mihi temerarium & nimium audax videtur, cum ingenii nostri tenuitas divinae potentiae, & sapientiae abyssum penetrare & scrutari non valeat: nec ea res sit satis ratione percepta, aut sat distincte in sacra Scriptura revelata.
pass_a_gloss: As far as concerns me, I judge the modesty of these most Learned Men greatly to be praised: and to define for certain the mode of the divine concurrence, by which the first cooperates with second causes, seems to me rash and too bold, since the slenderness of our wit is not able to penetrate and search the abyss of divine power, and wisdom: nor is that matter sufficiently perceived by reason, or revealed distinctly enough in sacred Scripture.
pass_b_english: For my part, I think the modesty of these very learned men deserves the highest praise. To define with certainty the manner of divine concurrence by which the first cause cooperates with secondary causes seems to me rash and far too bold.
Our feeble understanding cannot penetrate and search out the abyss of God's power and wisdom, and the matter is neither adequately grasped by reason nor revealed clearly enough in Holy Scripture.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
